correctness.rationale: Dirichlet uniform-spacings exchangeability gives a uniform subset of c-1 internal breaks conditional on C_n=c. Marked composition counts give (c)_A J(n-S,c-A)/J(n,c) at all feasible finite n, including c=n. For c~a sqrt(n), exact falling-factorial algebra gives a^{2A}, the mixed factorial moments of independent Poisson(a²) counts; tightness and moment determination prove joint convergence for any fixed K. At r_n=(log n+x)/(2n), E(C_n-1)~e^{-x/2}sqrt(n), and negatively correlated Dirichlet gap indicators give Var(C_n)<=E(C_n-1)=O(sqrt(n)); conditioning completes the theorem. The actual standalone verify.py passed 5345 exact finite assertions. Finite checks are not used to infer the infinity limit.

value.rationale: At the known isolation threshold, every fixed component cardinality—not just isolated nodes—has an equally intense nonzero Poisson limiting count, and all finitely many such counts become independent despite a growing total component population. This is a natural complete rare-component profile relevant to connectivity failure mechanisms, with an exact finite-n factorial-moment law enabling calibration at arbitrary radii. The result does not rely on an unmotivated parameter slice; it evaluates the canonical isolation transition in the widely studied fixed-sample geometric model.
